Question Choices: Find the Least Common Multiplier (LCM) of 6 and 14 using Prime Factorization.
Solution: 42     ->  We break both numbers into prime factors and take all the factors needed (using the biggest amount of each) so the number can be divided by both and is the smallest possible. 6 = 2 * 3,14 = 2 * 7, so LCM = 2 x 3 x 7 = 42
